 Follow New NOAA Winter Storm Map Forecasts ‘Heavy Snow’ For 3 States Next Week
 Matthew Thomas Sat, November 7, 2026 at 12:15 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. A newly released map from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration reveals where "heavy snow" is forecast to arrive in three states next week. Learn more about where the early winter weather could strike in the coming days and how much snow may be expected.
 The 3 States Where 'Heavy Snow' Is Forecast Next Week
 Official weather prediction chart from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration illustrating severe weather contours across the United States.Photo credit: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration/NOAA.gov
 On November 6, 2026, NOAA's Climate Prediction Center published its U.S. Hazards Outlook Map for November 14 through 20. It forecasted that the area outlined in pink could be hit with "heavy snow" on November 14 and 15. The map includes a major part of Eastern and Northern California, a region in Southern Oregon, and part of Western Nevada in the pink zone.
 While the map didn't outline how many inches of snow could fall, NOAA has a specific definition of the term " heavy snow " that can be found on its website. It states that four or more inches must fall in 12 hours or six or more inches within 24 hours to qualify as "heavy snow" by the agency.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Alongside the map, the Climate Prediction Center also published a description of the forecast for the pink areas outlined in the image. It details that there is a "moderate risk" of heavy snow at high elevations across the Klamath Mountains and the Sierra Nevada Mountains on November 14 and 15. It also describes a "slight risk" of heavy snow at high elevations across the Cascades and parts of the Northern Intermountain, Great Basin, and Central and Northern Rockies between November 14 and 17.
 Considering that the Klamath Mountains and the Sierra Nevada Mountains are home to several ski resorts , the forecasted "heavy snow" will be a reason to rejoice for many people. Between the owners of those resorts and skiing enthusiasts, there is always a lot of interest in potential early winter storms that promise to add inches to the snowpack if they arrive.
